page.layout: One column of running text, with fragmentary marginal notes down the right margin, mostly cut off and illegible. Running head at top centre. Page number at top right. Catchword at right below the last line. Gathering signature "C" at bottom left.

main_text.p: rum inprimis & acre erat,excitatis quoque publicâ præconis voce ad accusationem ipsorum æmulis, si fine labe reperirentur, ut tum demum honos ille iis tribueretur. Venerandum enim hunc senatum, atque ideò labis omnis expertem esse voluit, qui summam autoritatem in totâ civitate esset habiturus.

Quam ob rem non alios quàm in maximis reipublicæ negociis jam antè ver-satos, rerumque summarum peritos, & culpæ infamiæque exfortes senatores in eo esse fivit. Nam {ἐφόρεων} ac {ἐπι-σκοπῶν} intendentem in omnes reipu-blicæ partes legumque ac institutorum bonorum confervationem ei tribuit, & avertendorum obrepentium vitiorum curam demandavit. Quinetiam cognitionem ac judicium gravissimorum criminum, cædis confultò patratæ, venefi-cii, incendii, proditionis, ac similium quæ capitis poenam merebantur, eidem[illegible, ~6 letters] dedit. Denique cenfuram morum ac vitæ omnium civium, maximè verò juniorum, senatui huic affignavit. Quo capite muneris sui fretus hic idem senatus, quid quisque civium ageret, quo quæstu se fuofque fuftentaret inquifivit, ignaviæ ac inertis otii, item petulantiæ nequitiæve compertos, poenâ affecit: adeò ut memoriæ proditum sit,

page.notes: Right margin: several fragmentary marginal notes are present (for example near "reipu-", "bonorum", "cri-minum", "quæ capitis", "Quo capite", "quæstu", "petu-lantiæ"), but they are cut off by the binding edge and are mostly illegible. Only one is transcribed, as a placeholder; the rest could not be read. Greek words are doubtful: "ἐφόρεων" and "ἐπισκοπῶν" are uncertain readings of the printed Greek. The line-end hyphens in "ver-satos" and "reipu-blicæ" are as printed. The red-tinted right edge is a scan or binding artefact, not text. The catchword "teste-" is partly obscured and uncertain.
